title: After the City’s watch-list rating: what the State and Washington awarded next
question: When the City’s Controller puts a grantee on its watch list, do other public funders keep awarding it new money?
finding: The Controller’s reports for fiscal 2019 to 2025 name 24 profiled organizations as elevated concern, red flag, tier 2 or tier 3. 6 of them have State or federal awards dated after the fiscal year of their first rating: $35.0 million from the State and $9.1 million from federal agencies, beside $19.4 million of federal subawards from the City itself. The largest: Friendship House Assoc of American India (Tier 2, fiscal 2024; then Department of Health Care Services: The Village SF Wellness Center ($31.4 million, 2025-05-06)); PRC (Red Flag, fiscal 2022; then Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development: California Community Reinvestment Grants Program ($3.0 million, 2024-06-01)); Baker Places Inc (Red Flag, fiscal 2022; then Department of Health and Human Services: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Projects ($2.5 million, 2022-09-15)).
how: Ratings are the Controller’s printed lists (37 rows, with page references). State awards are California Grants Portal rows dated by project start (or the start of the State fiscal year where none is given); federal awards are USAspending prime grants and contracts by first action date, and subawards by action date. An award counts when dated on or after 1 July following the fiscal year of the first rating. Names are matched on the normalised name; 1 printed names matched no profile (United Council of Human Services).
limits: A City rating is about fiscal and compliance monitoring and is not by itself a bar on funding; the last two columns show the City’s own payments continuing. Other funders apply their own tests, a State capital grant is decided on a building plan and may have been applied for before the rating, and a federal renewal follows a multi-year award. The records do not show whether the State or the federal agency knew of the City rating; the award file and the application’s disclosure questions would. State and federal rows carry no number in common with the City’s files: each is tied by the same name plus a second key, San Francisco as the county served (State) or a San Francisco recipient address (federal). Where that second key is thin, the records do not show whether it is the same organisation or two with the same name; the award file would settle it.
